headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line while ETF buyers show up anyway
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it answers the only question that matters before you look at anything else: none of the seven assets on the board, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, ADA, are above their 200-day line. That's a fully aligned downtrend structure across the majors. BTC sits 49% off its 12-month high of $124,773.51 at $63,653.85, and the damage scales up from there: ETH is 60.6% off its high, SOL 70.4%, DOGE 75.7%, ADA a stark 83.2% off its own 12-month peak. When every cross agrees like this, it's not noise from one weak coin, it's the whole board reading the same way.

Momentum is where it gets more interesting, because it isn't confirming the trend so much as sitting on its hands. BTC's RSI-14 is 47.4, dead center, MACD below signal. ETH's RSI is actually the strongest of the group at 56.3 despite being furthest below its high in percentage terms, and it's up 6.36% over 30 days and 1.81% over seven, the only asset on the board with a green 7-day and 30-day print. That's a real divergence worth naming: ETH is technically below its 200-day and its MACD is below signal too, but price action over the past month has been quietly constructive while BTC has drifted sideways to down (-2.97% 30-day). Meanwhile SOL and DOGE show the weakest momentum, RSI 42.7 and 40.7 respectively, with DOGE also carrying the worst 30-day return at -19.15%.

The rest of the pack, XRP, BNB, ADA, sit in that same 42-48 RSI band: not oversold, not confirming anything, just resting.

Positioning tells a story of a market that's mostly calm but leaning long into weak spots. BTC funding is barely positive at 0.7% annualized, cheap to hold a long, and its long/short ratio of 1.37 isn't crowded. ETH funding is actually negative (-3.5% annualized), meaning shorts are paying longs there, an unusual tell in a market with the best 30-day return on the board. The real crowding shows up further out the risk curve: DOGE's long/short ratio is 5.19, XRP's is 3.69, both paying meaningfully positive funding (7.7% and 7.8% annualized) to stay long. That's a lot of one-sided money in the smaller names. Liquidations back this up unevenly: BTC's 21-hour window shows shorts getting hurt far more than longs ($5.24M vs $539K), while ETH's book is close to balanced ($4.33M longs vs $4.06M shorts). Crowded and expensive in DOGE and XRP is a fragile setup; BTC's flat funding is comparatively cheap fuel either way.

Flows are where the tape actively disagrees with the price action. On 17 Aug 2026, BTC spot ETFs took in $297.5M net, but the five-session net is only $56.9M and same_direction_days sits at 1, so this is one strong day sitting on top of a choppier stretch, not a running streak. ETH ETFs added $30.9M on the same day with a firmer $42.5M over five sessions. Underneath that, whale wallets moved a net $29,017,855 off exchanges in the last 48 hours, continuing a shift: the weekly net figures show two big inflow-to-exchange weeks ($1.01B, $1.10B) followed by two outflow weeks (-$407M, -$296M), a real reversal in trend direction. Add $129.9M in USDT specifically moving onto Bitfinex, tagged as stablecoin buying power sitting at the ready, against BTC leaving exchanges toward cold storage (the single largest move was $176.99M off Bitstamp). Stablecoin float itself is essentially flat, down just 0.58% over 30 days at $306.48B, so this isn't dry powder evaporating, it's parked.

Sentiment is sitting at 41, Fear, near the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 41. So the crowd has been more fearful recently than it is right now, but it's still fear, not greed. That sits oddly next to a day where BTC ETFs printed their strongest single day of net inflow in the window given, and whales pulled coin off exchanges rather than toward them. The tape and the mood gauge aren't singing the same tune today. What's worth watching from here: whether ETF same_direction_days extends beyond one (a real streak, not a one-off print), whether XRP and DOGE funding cools off from their current 7-8% annualized levels as long/short ratios above 3 and 5 respectively are the kind of crowding that unwinds hard in either direction, and whether any major actually reclaims its 200-day line, which none have done yet.
